Spec 1f61f624 (phase 3) constrains: "The notification set is a function of the STATE CHANGE, not of who performed it: exactly TWO notificationService.create calls for SUBMITTED and APPROVED cancellations, exactly ONE for DRAFT" and "Self-notification is not suppressed: when the cancelling actor is the resolved recipient, the notification is still written. The phase-6 spec (9244f013) constrains "Additive extension only: every pre-existing test case ... must remain byte-for-byte in intent — no case deleted, renamed, skipped, or weakened", and its success criterion #3 requires "a DRAFT cancellation still produces EXACTLY ONE notification (requester only) — the pre-existing DRAFT assertion is unchanged and no approver notification is added on that path." findings.quoted_line: - **`leave_requests`** (UNCHANGED, referenced by name) — already carries `status`, `approver_id`, `cancelled_by`, `cancelled_at`, `reverses_request_id`. New indexes: standalone `status` (the existing `(employee_id, status)` cannot serve a status-only predicate — this is the first status-only access path in the codebase) and `approver_id` (recipient resolution for a cancelled APPROVED request). The queue query MUST also exclude `reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL`: a cancelled-after-approval request is TWO rows, so without that predicate the reversal row is a spurious second queue entry. **NOT delivered as of Phase 1** — the delivered migration adds no `leave_requests` DDL at all; see *Phase 1 delivered* below.

findings.message:
[review/stale-spec] Stale placement of recipient resolution. `docs/DECISIONS.md` → ADR-003 records the opposite and gives the reason: "Resolving the recipient inside the `withTransaction` callback: `IEmployeeService.getEmployeeById` takes no `PoolClient`, so the employee read cannot join the transaction ... Resolution is therefore hoisted above `uow.withTransaction`, and only the notification INSERT joins it." The built code matches ADR-003 — `const approverRecipient = await this.resolveApproverRecipient(request);` sits above `return this.uow.withTransaction(...)`. Change "and inside the same callback" to "before the unit of work opens".
  Evidence: "**Transaction.** Cancelling a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request performs, in ONE unit of work: (a) the status change — an in-place `update` to CANCELLED for SUBMITTED, or the GP-008 insert of a NEW CANCELLED reversal row for APPROVED; (b) the balance release — `pendingDays -= requestedDays` for SUBMITTED, `usedDays -= requestedDays` for …
findings.quoted_line: **Transaction.** Cancelling a SUBMITTED or APPROVED request performs, in ONE unit of work: (a) the status change — an in-place `update` to CANCELLED for SUBMITTED, or the GP-008 insert of a NEW CANCELLED reversal row for APPROVED; (b) the balance release — `pendingDays -= requestedDays` for SUBMITTED, `usedDays -= requestedDays` for APPROVED; (c) the CANCEL audit entry (unchanged in shape); (d) the approver notification insert. Repository and service methods that must join a caller's transaction take an OPTIONAL trailing `client?: PoolClient` defaulting to the shared pool. `LeaveService.cancel` calls `this.uow.withTransaction(async (client) => { ... })`; `PgUnitOfWork` acquires a client, issues BEGIN, runs the callback, COMMITs on resolve / ROLLBACKs on throw, and always releases the client. Inside the callback the SAME `client` is threaded to every participating call. `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` appear ONLY in `PgUnitOfWork`. The approver is resolved before the notification insert and inside the same callback: for an APPROVED request, `request.approverId` read from the ORIGINAL row (the reversal row's `approverId` is null by construction); for a SUBMITTED request, `employeeService.getEmployeeById(request.employeeId).managerId`.

findings.message: [review/documentation] ADR-004's central premise is factually wrong, and it is the premise the whole ADR (and its "load-bearing comment" consequence) rests on. Fastify 4.29.1 — the version pinned in package-lock.json — uses find-my-way 8.2.2, which matches static nodes ahead of parametric ones irrespective of registration order; its README states "static routes are always inserted before parametric and wildcard" and lists the match order as "1. static 2. parametric node with static ending ...". Verified by execution against the pinned versions: registering `GET /leaves/:id` FIRST and `GET /leaves/pending-decisions` SECOND, then injecting `GET /leaves/pending-decisions`, returns 200 from the static handler — not the 404 via `getById` this ADR claims. The same holds when the routes are registered inside a `leaveRoutes(fastify)` plugin. So "a static path registered after a parametric sibling is shadowed by it" and "resolves as `id = 'pending-decisions'`, reaches `getById`, and returns …
